decision.status: Expert-store split-state correctness passes; general incremental session reuse remains provisional
decision.reason: Both expert-store implementations are bit-exact under the same split-state execution, and both are bit-exact under one-pass execution. Split state and one-pass history produced the same 64 greedy tokens but measurably different logits from step zero. Because the difference is upstream execution-boundary behavior and the corpus has only one boundary case, vference must not claim general output invariance for arbitrary incremental multi-turn reuse yet.
decision.safe_default: Do not expose incremental multi-turn state reuse as a qualified default until a broader boundary corpus passes predefined token/state tolerances. Stateless transcript rendering and one-pass prefill remain the conservative application behavior.
decision.quality_scope: No vference storage/cache behavior changed logits. The remaining question is whether the pinned Qwen/MLX segmented-state numerics preserve outputs broadly enough for a session API.
